Based on the retrieved excerpts, the safety committee's position is supported by **ISO 45001 clause 5.4** (Doc 1).

**Clause 5.4** explicitly requires the organization to establish processes for "consultation and participation of workers at all levels and functions" in the **development, planning, implementation, performance evaluation and improvement actions** of the OH&S system. The clause specifically mandates giving **"special emphasis to the involvement of non-managerial workers"** and removing barriers such as "fear of reprisal."

Since incident investigation constitutes both **performance evaluation** and drives **improvement actions**, this clause directly supports including shop-floor workers—not just supervisors—on investigation teams. The requirement for "special emphasis" on non-managerial worker involvement further strengthens the committee's case, as shop-floor workers would bring direct operational knowledge that supervisors may lack.

Additionally, **clause 5.1** (Doc 3) reinforces this by requiring top management to demonstrate leadership through actions including "protecting workers from reprisals when they report incidents," which supports creating an environment where workers can participate meaningfully in investigations without fear.
